what.summary: Free, residential career training and education for low-income young adults aged 16 through 24.

evidence.quote: Job Corps is the nation’s largest free, residential career training and education program for low-income young adults ages 16 through 24.

pay.summary: Students receive a living allowance every two weeks that rises as training progresses, and pay nothing for the program.

evidence.quote: Throughout your training, you will receive a biweekly basic living allowance. As your training progresses, your living allowance will increase.
Job Corps is always FREE for students. The program is fully funded by the federal government.

who.summary: Generally low-income 16- through 24-year-olds who are U.S. citizens, legal residents, residents of a U.S. territory or authorized to work in the United States.

evidence.quote: Generally, Job Corps students are low-income 16- through 24-year-olds who are U.S. citizens, legal U.S. residents or residents of a U.S. territory, and/or individuals who are authorized to work in the United States.

apply.summary: Start by creating a MyJobCorps account.

evidence.quote: The first step in applying to Job Corps is creating a MyJobCorps account.
